title: 1990 AHSME Problem 17
statement: How many of the numbers \(100,\) \(101,\) \(\ldots,\) \(999\) have three different digits in increasing order or in decreasing order?

solutions.text:
An increasing three-digit number cannot use \(0,\) so there are \(\binom93=84\) increasing numbers. Any three digits chosen from \(0\) through \(9\) form a valid decreasing three-digit number, because the largest digit comes first; this gives \(\binom{10}{3}=120.\) The total is \(84+120=204.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Choosing three distinct digits fixes their increasing or decreasing order
Treat the digit \(0\) carefully in the increasing case
